# Urbicon UI

> Svelte 5 component library with built-in i18n, OKLCH design tokens, and AI-native developer experience.

## Overview

Urbicon UI is a Svelte 5 + Tailwind CSS 4 component library designed for LLM-assisted development. It uses a custom zero-dependency `tv()` variant engine for styling, a three-layer OKLCH token system for automatic dark mode, and provides production-ready primitives and patterns.

## Quick Start

Packages are published on the public npm registry — no registry configuration needed, just install:

```bash
bun add @urbicon-ui/blocks
```

Then two CSS imports — Tailwind first, then the token sheet (it also carries the `@source`
directives that make the components' classes reachable):

```css
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import '@urbicon-ui/blocks/style/index.css';
```

Requirements: Svelte 5, Vite and Tailwind 4. SvelteKit is **not** required — `blocks`, `table` and
`i18n` import neither `$app/*` nor `@sveltejs/kit`. Import the stylesheet where your app loads CSS
(`+layout.svelte` under SvelteKit, `main.js` in a plain Vite + Svelte app).

In a SvelteKit project the `sv` add-on does both steps at once — non-interactive form for CI and
agents, so Tailwind's plugin prompt never blocks the run. It is the one SvelteKit-only piece; in a
non-Kit project use the two steps above:

```bash
bunx sv add tailwindcss=plugins:none @urbicon-ui
```

```svelte
<script>
  import { Button, Input, Card } from '@urbicon-ui/blocks';
</script>

<Card variant="elevated" padding="md">
  <Input label="Name" placeholder="Enter name" />
  <Button intent="primary" variant="filled">Submit</Button>
</Card>
```

## Documentation

- [Full API Reference](llms-full.txt): Complete component props, variants, tokens, and patterns
- [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md): Token system, Mint interactions, i18n, docs-gen pipeline
- [API Conventions](docs/COMPONENT-API-CONVENTIONS.md): Props patterns, callbacks, styling rules
- [Component Structure](docs/ComponentStructureStandard.md): File layout, index.ts pattern

## Components

- **Layout**: Card, Dialog, Popover, Tooltip, Separator, Accordion
- **Actions**: Button, ButtonGroup, Toolbar, Menu, Combobox
- **Forms**: Input, Checkbox, Toggle
- **Feedback**: Badge, Spinner, Pagination, Alert, Toast, Skeleton
- **Navigation**: Tab, Breadcrumb
- **Display**: Avatar
- **Help / Guidance**: Guide, GuidePanel, GuideHint, GuideMarker, GuideMention, GuideBeacon (bidirectional in-app help: opt-in spotlight tour, contextual hints, non-modal help panel, UI↔guide links)

## Key Patterns

All components share: `intent`, `size`, `variant`, `unstyled`, `slotClasses`, `preset`, `mint`, `class` props.
For project-wide styling, `BlocksProvider` accepts `defaults` (every instance), named `presets` (opt-in), and prop-conditional `overrides` (e.g. style only `variant="outlined"`).
Import from `@urbicon-ui/blocks`. Use semantic tokens (`bg-surface-base`, not `bg-white`). Use `focus-visible:` for focus styles.

## Agent Tooling

One dev-dependency, `@urbicon-ui/design`, ships the `urbicon` CLI: version-pinned component
knowledge (`urbicon primer` / `find` / `get-component`) and a deterministic design linter
(`urbicon validate`) that runs as an edit-time hook and CI gate; `bunx urbicon init` wires a
project in. Ask the CLI rather than reading the package sources. One measurement (Haiku 4.5, one
task, CLI plus edit-time gate against neither): reading the package it shipped 373 linter
findings, mostly raw Tailwind colours and hand-written `dark:` overrides; with CLI and gate,
`urbicon validate` came out clean. Design quality was unchanged either way — this buys token
discipline, not taste.
